description: Cross-driver vectors for a personal final_result entry against a bundled correction of the same trigger: the output of a final entry is never matched again, a final entry that changes nothing still claims its text, and a final end-character entry of higher priority holds back a lower immediate one. Replayed by the Windows engine and dispatcher, the macOS expander and the shared engine on Linux; every driver must reach the same screen.

field_semantics.matrix: Every combination of the axes is replayed: a personal rule (priority 100, final_result, word_start) against a bundled rule `trigger` > `bundled` (priority 10, not final, word_start, not case sensitive). Typing the trigger then the end character must leave the personal output plus the end character on screen.
field_semantics.personal_auto: Whether the personal rule fires on its own last character.
field_semantics.bundled_auto: Whether the bundled rule fires on its own last character.
field_semantics.case_sensitive: The editor's case box: is_case_sensitive and is_case_sensitive_strict on the personal rule.
field_semantics.output: The personal rule's output: identical to the trigger, a case variant of it, or different text.
field_semantics.max_arrows: hotstrings.cascade_max_arrows, 1 being no chaining at all.
field_semantics.end_char: The word delimiter typed after the trigger.
field_semantics.rules: Explicit vectors: registered hotstrings. auto: fires on its own last character; word_start: only at the start of a word; priority: collision priority; final_result; case_sensitive: is_case_sensitive and is_case_sensitive_strict.
field_semantics.typed: The characters typed, in order; a Space, Tab or Enter is an end character.
field_semantics.expect_screen: The text left in the application.

vectors.description: Typing the output itself: the final entry changes nothing and still claims the text.
The same with an end-character personal entry.
Forgetting a final output does not disable the rule for the next word.
A final entry that changes nothing claims its own text, not what is typed after it.
The claim lasts for the very next key: a later occurrence behind other text is judged afresh.
Genuine chaining: the next key completes a trigger through the output.
The same rules with a final first entry: its output completes nothing.
A personal entry that is not final stays open to the correction on the end character.
Only a final entry of strictly higher priority holds an immediate one back.
An end-character entry that is not final keeps the rule that an immediate entry fires first.
